text: Great food in the buffet and comfy atmosphere. The view of the river valley isn't bad either.

The food was not inedible, except the crusty appetizers that had clearly been sitting on the buffet since lunch. And they advertise their kababs but none came with the buffet. Fresh naan was delivered and that was quite good. 

The "waiter" was grim, but responsive. The capper is  that they have their own brand of beer, a light lager, but I wanted something else (we were already regretting our restaurant choice so I was leery about the beer) I asked him for a menu with their selection of beers (East Asian Village has a wonderful selection of beer) and ordered a Kingfisher. A man, I assumed to be an owner, came over and told me they have only ONE beer, their own brand. He brought me 330 ml of beer in a elderly looking pint glass that was clearly bought at a thrift store. We couldn't get out of there soon enough.

So I had been wondering about the semi-brand change from New Asian Village to The Great Indian Factory, and well I wonder no more as the buffet here is really quite good. Now, I will say that as a cilantro-hater, I did have to play the cilantro avoidance game a bit, but that is only to be expected at an Indian buffet. I really liked the butter chicken, the cheese, the cinnamon naan, and the fresh naan and sauces! I also rather enjoyed the half pot of chai tea I ordered and drank throughout the meal. Yes I overate a bit due to it being a buffet but I so enjoyed my food! 

The kabob of the evening was delivered directly to our table which was a good touch. As was the naan and beverages. The buffet was well lit and each dish was labeled with the ingredients including whether it was vegan friendly or nut-free. This seemed nice although the grammar was occasionally poor on signage throughout the restaurant. The food quality was good and staff were really helpful and welcoming. 

I would be happy to return here if my experiences continue to be this good!

This place is overpriced and not that good. The naan is brought to your table but it's thin stale and hard like a pita. There really isn't a whole lot of curry selection and they all kinda taste the same or bland. I think they are trying to mirror a chain restaurant in India in the Radisson Hotels where they bring you kebabs (endless and various kinds) as an appetizer and then you get your curries from a buffet. This is not that! They come with only one skewer and it takes some time so you get it way later into your meal. For 24 dollars this place wasn't worth it at all.

We had lunch at the Great Indian Factory on Saskatchewan Drive today.  Oddly, though we were told that they were not affiliated with The New Asian Village (they occupy the old location), they still have the framed awards, etc. of the New Asian Village posted prominently above the buffet tables!  We were told they will be opening 3 more locations soon.

I found the food fairly tasty, though my wife said she thought some of the dishes were only luke-warm in temperature (she complained that the rice was cold) and not really that spicy. A refill of the water glass resulted in water of tepid temperature.

Looks like they or the previous owners put in new toilets, at least in the Men's Room as the new elongated toilets blocked the stall door from opening completely.  It's a bit unpleasant having to squeeze in through a partially open door to stand inches from the toilet, and then have to close the door in order to use the facilities, then repeat the gymnastics in reverse to exit the stall!  How hard would it have been to cut off a  1/2" or inch of the door or frame to allow for a full swing of the door?

A real surprise was when we got the check.  Though we showed him the SUTP discount coupon when we were first seated and the coupon clearly stated "2 for 1", we were only given $12.99 off the second meal which was $16.99!  We were told that the coupon states "subject to conditions" which apparently they can decide without telling you, The waiter could certainly have clarified this as we were being seated when we could then have decided whether to stay or not. This isn't being completely honest with your customers.

We likely won't return based on our overall experience, and unless some changes are made, their other proposed locations may have a hard go of it as well.

Been here twice. The first was after the grand re-opening. The food was superb then. Fresh, hot, tasty and we were treated to a complimentary drink and kabab. The next time on a Sunday evening.the food was still good and we were given a chicken kabab but the salads were lacking and the desserts were a mess. There were only two salads offered. The gulab jamin were crushed flat and in pieces in the steam table and the mango custard was very short on sweetness. Also there were no dessert spoons. Maybe someone having an off day.

First thing to note is that we went for the buffet. I'm only reviewing the buffet and comparing it to other buffet, not to a a la carte restaurant. 

That being out of the Way,  let's talk about the food. The food is really good. It's is full of flavors like indian food should be. Their Safran rice is excellent. The broth of their chicken soup tastes like it ws done with chicken bones, not like a powder. Their Naan bred tastes so fresh. You get it delivered to your table still hot from the oven. It's soft and simply delicious.

I also took one of their salad. It looked innocent enough but the cucumber pieces in it were suprising spicy. The lamb sauce tasted good but the met itself was a bit too hard for my taste. Service ws friendly and quick.

One last thing to mention about the buffet. It start at 5pm. Don't go there mid afternoon for the buffet. Only the a la carte is available at that time.

even one star is too much for this place...the worst desi food in town...it is the old new asian village resturant..under a new name...the food is terrible..not only terrible but old too...the place is suppose to be specializing in kababs...but not only a single kabab in rhe buffet....23 dollars for such terrible buffet...waste of money and time...a total mood killer...not recommended at all....

This place is authentic and delicious 
It is s must for Indian food

They have a buffet with too many things to count. I have gone for lunch and then returned the same night for dinner

This restaurant serves one of the best Indian cuisine that I have had the pleasure to eat in Edmonton. Their spread; the quality and taste of the food is next to none, in my opinion.
Since I discovered it a few months ago, it has become my kitchen away from home. Additionally, the location is prime just overlooking downtown through the river valley. 
I seriously recommend it to anybody looking for some rich Indian/well spiced dinning experience.

I will going back there as many times as possible, as long as I am in this city.
